description: Dominance pruning removes search nodes in decoupled search, where each node holds a center state and a *price* (cheapest cost) for every reachable leaf state. A new node is pruned if a stored node with the same center *dominates* it: the stored node can do all that the new one can, at no higher total cost. The basic test compares prices directly; stronger tests compare only the leaf states that can still matter (the *frontier*), lower prices that cannot pay off (*effective prices*), or let a leaf state stand in for another that it *simulates*. Without such pruning, prices can grow forever along center cycles, so the search may not stop on unsolvable tasks; with it the search terminates and stays optimal.

papers.authors: Álvaro Torralba, Daniel Gnad, Patrick Dubbert, Jörg Hoffmann
papers.title: On State-Dominance Criteria in Fork-Decoupled Search
papers.venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence (IJCAI)
